header: What a week at Atlas actually looks like
subheadline: No account managers, no timesheets billed in six-minute blocks, and nothing shown to a client before someone outside the project has taken it apart. Three habits carry most of that, and all three are older than the Berlin studio.

items.title: Thursday critique
items.description: Every project puts unfinished work on the wall at 15:00 on Thursday. Nobody presents, everybody argues, and the file is back on the desk by Friday.

items.title: Two weeks in the field first
items.description: Discovery starts on site: depots, branch counters, ward rounds. Screens come after the notes, and the notes stay with the client.

items.title: Designers talk to clients
items.description: Whoever drew the screen explains it. There is no account layer between the studio and the people paying the invoice.
